ios.desc:
You're on the go. Someone's giving you directions, or a phone number, name of a restaurant... you need to write it down now, quickly!

No time to create new contact, or a note, a file, or waste time on additional taps, bring up keyboard... You just need to write it somewhere right now.

*scratch* is a simple scratch pad.

• No bells or whistles, just a simple area to quickly jot something down.
• Launch *scratch* and write.
• Quickly create lists or checkboxes.
• All plain text.
• Share to other apps or save to Files as an org file (plain text).
• No cloud, account, sign-in, or social required.

Bonus: Emacs org mode lovers, you can use lightweight org markup like headings, plain lists, numbered lists, and checkboxes.

show_hn.title: Show HN: *scratch* – A minimal org mode scratch area for iOS

quotes.text:
I've written a handful iOS apps powered by org. Journelly is my latest https://xenodium.com/journelly-like-tweeting-but-for-your-eyes-only

I got quite a few users who either come from Markdown or simply don't care about the internal implementation. Here's a wonderful writeup by a user https://ellanew.com/ptpl/157-2025-05-19-journelly-is-org-for-those-who-dont-do-org

ps. Markdown is also coming to Journelly https://xenodium.com/markdown-is-coming-to-journelly

edit: My other org-based iOS apps

- Flat Habits (habits tracker): https://flathabits.com

- Plain Org (general purpose org viewer/editor): https://plainorg.com

- Scratch (a scratch buffer): https://apps.apple.com/us/app/scratch/id1671420139

I’m seeing scratch solutions shared, so here’s mine for iOS

https://apps.apple.com/gb/app/scratch/id1671420139

I tried to optimise for least number of taps to quickly write something down.

Here’s a blog post by a user
https://irreal.org/blog/?p=11202
